item.title: Development of the LIMB-QOL measurement system
item.content:encoded:
Jessica Roydhouse, Menzies Institute for Medical Research

Brittany Lapin, Cleveland Clinic

This special collection presents foundational research on the LIMB-QOL, a comprehensive patient-reported outcome measurement system designed to evaluate multiple dimensions of health and functioning in individuals who have experienced limb loss or severe extremity trauma. Developed through a collaborative effort supported by the U.S. Department of Defense, the system addresses physical, emotional, and social wellbeing across diverse populations with major extremity injuries.

The collection welcomes manuscripts that contribute to understanding the development, validation, and clinical application of this measurement framework, intended for both researchers and healthcare practitioners working with extremity trauma patients.

Appel publié par Quality of Life Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Patient-reported outcomes for limb loss and extremity trauma
  • Development and validation of the Limb Injury Measurement Battery for Quality of Life
  • Measurement of physical, emotional, and social health domains in individuals with major extremity injuries
  • Implementation of LIMB-QOL in clinical and research settings
  • Quality of life assessment methodologies for traumatic injury populations

item.title: Enhancing Population Health Assessment: Key Papers from the EQ-DAPHNIE Project
item.content:encoded:
Brittany Lapin, Cleveland Clinic

Jessica Roydhouse, Menzies Institute for Medical Research

The EQ-DAPHNIE project is a major population health assessment initiative funded by the EuroQol Research Foundation that collected comprehensive health data including demographics, social determinants, and patient-reported outcome measures from 15 countries. This special collection brings together research examining the diverse findings and applications of this dataset across multiple health assessment contexts.

Appel publié par Quality of Life Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Population norms for patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs)
  • Cross-country comparisons of health assessment instruments
  • Health inequalities examination
  • Instrument performance assessment within and across countries
  • Self-reported health analysis
  • Efficacy of health measures in elderly populations
  • Generic and symptom-specific PROMs evaluation

item.title: Patient experience data in regulatory and health technology assessment
item.content:encoded:
Wen-Hung Chen, AstraZeneca

Lori D. McLeod, RTI Health Solutions

Regulatory and health technology assessment bodies increasingly recognize the value of incorporating patient perspectives during product development and evaluation. Patient experience data encompasses patient-reported outcomes, clinical assessments, and preference information, yet their integration into decision-making remains inconsistent. This collection seeks to advance understanding of how different stakeholders approach patient experience data to ensure patient voices meaningfully influence healthcare decisions.

The collection invites original research, reviews, and discussion papers examining how patient experience data—including preferences, symptoms, and quality of life measures—can inform regulatory and HTA submissions and decisions. Contributions addressing recent developments in the field and exploring emerging applications such as artificial intelligence and digital health technologies in patient experience research are particularly encouraged.

Appel publié par Quality of Life Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Assessment of patient experience, preferences, symptoms, and health-related quality of life for regulatory and HTA submissions
  • Patient-reported outcomes and clinical outcome assessments in product development and evaluation
  • Patient preference information collection and evaluation
  • Artificial intelligence and digital health technology applications in patient experience data research
  • Regulatory and HTA developments and decision-making processes
  • Integration of patient voices in healthcare decisions to improve patient outcomes

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Submission deadline
